subject: Clarify: requested log preservation scope and evidence for SIG/SOC2
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <security@novaclinic.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request re: log preservation window for SIG questionnaire

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick chat earlier. As we work through the SIG questionnaire for our upcoming audit, our InfoSec team needs clarity on Redwood's log retention guarantees and whether Novaclinic can request longer preservation for specific log classes.

We have two asks:
- Can Redwood support a customer-specific preservation period of 18 months for security/forensics logs (audit, auth, and request traces)?
- If yes, what evidence can you provide that shows deletion workflows are enforced (proof of deletion, retention policy, snapshot/backup retention windows, and role separation for log access)?

For our internal auditors we'd like: a short description of how logs are retained and deleted (policy + automated workflows), a copy of the most recent SOC 2 summary that references log controls, and a sample of the retention exception template you would use.

We appreciate a response within 7 business days if possible — our audit timeline is tight. I'm cc'ing procurement (Tom Green) who will coordinate any formal amendment to the MSA if we need to scope an exception.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Information Security Manager
Novaclinic Health
security@novaclinic.com

(attachment: sig_questionnaire_section_log_retention.xlsx)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <security@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request re: log preservation window for SIG questionnaire

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the attached SIG excerpt. We can definitely walk through options.

Quick answers up front:
- We have a standard retention baseline (30 days for request traces, 90 days for operational logs, 365 days for audit logs).
- We can discuss a scoped, customer-specific preservation accommodation for forensic/audit logs with compensating controls — this is not the default.

Next steps so we don't block your audit:
1) Marissa (Compliance) — can you assemble a short evidence packet: policy summary, SOC 2 item references, and the retention exception template?
2) Ben — please add deal context and whether Novaclinic is requesting a contractual amendment or just evidence for auditors.
3) Elena — can you confirm exactly which log classes (e.g., auth, request traces, K/V cache diagnostics, system metrics) you need to preserve for 18 months? That will help scope the exception.

I've attached our retention overview and the high-level SOC 2 summary for context — will follow with a scoped exception draft once we confirm log classes.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

(attachments: redwood_retention_overview_v1.pdf, soc2_audit_summary_2026.pdf)

Cc: Tom Green <procurement@novaclinic.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request re: log preservation window for SIG questionnaire — Proposed scope and evidence

Hi all,

Thanks for the patience — pulled together responses and an evidence bundle. Summary below, attachments included.

Summary of options (company position):
1) Standard offering (no contractual change):
   - Operational request traces: 30 days
   - System metrics and diagnostics: 90 days
   - Audit logs (access, auth, config changes): 365 days
   - Deletion workflow: automated TTL jobs with deletion audit events retained for 90 days

2) Scoped preservation accommodation (customer-specific amendment):
   - Proposal: allow Novaclinic to preserve a copy of "forensic/audit logs" for up to 18 months. Scope would be limited to logs classified as: access/auth events, admin/config change events, and request traces flagged for incident analysis.
   - Controls required:
     a) Encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed KMS (we support bring-your-own-kms on Private/Dedicated)
     b) Role-based access with quarterly access reviews and read-only export logs
     c) Retention exception documented and signed by procurement/legal
     d) Separate storage bucket with immutable object settings for the duration of retention (no accidental TTL applies)

Operational notes / caveats:
- Backups & snapshots: Our standard snapshot rotation is 30 days; the exception requires exporting scoped logs to the retention bucket. That export process is operationally manual/nearline and will be included in the amendment.
- Cost: there will be a modest monthly storage delta and an operational setup fee — Ben will coordinate pricing with procurement.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide deletion audit events and a signed retention exception when records are purged. For SOC 2 auditors we can provide screenshots of deletion audit events, a sample export manifest, and the retention exception record.

Attachments provided: novaclinic_evidence_bundle.zip (contains: retention_exception_template.docx, sample_deletion_audit_event.json, export_manifest_example.csv, high_level_runbook.md)

Next steps:
- Elena/Tom: confirm that the 18-month scope is limited to the log classes above and that Novaclinic will accept the controls listed.
- Rachel/Ben: if accepted, I'll prepare the formal amendment language and the evidence export checklist (ops runbook).

If helpful, I can set up a 30-minute working session with Ops to walk through the export flow and the retention bucket configuration.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

(attachments: novaclinic_evidence_bundle.zip, retention_exception_template.docx)
